analysis.title: Goldman Now Expects A Third Rate Hike In March 2027, Followed By Rate Cuts Starting In December 2027
key_insights: Goldman (David Mericle) adds a third 25bp Fed hike in March 2027, lifting the peak funds rate to 4.25-4.50%.
Goldman now expects the first Fed cut in December 2027 instead of September 2027, followed by cuts in March, June and September 2028.
October core CPI rose +0.30%, the third straight month of upside inflation surprises. The strength was broad across categories and went beyond direct pass-through from higher oil prices.
Goldman estimates the October CPI report implies a 35bp rise in core PCE prices for October.

Governor Waller said before the CPI release that his baseline is a 25bp December hike, but a 50bp hike should be considered if core CPI came in near 0.3% or higher, because moving only 25bp could put Fed credibility at risk.

Goldman still thinks most FOMC voters will be reluctant to move to a 50bp hike, but expects most participants to signal a third hike in the December dot plot. This would require only two more participants to raise their forecasts.
A third hike could come in January, but Goldman sees March as more likely because it expects softer inflation in November and December before the 'January effect' pushes inflation firmer again.

Oil futures have fallen substantially since the elections, so Goldman sees most of the energy pass-through to consumer prices as already behind us. It expects inflation to be meaningfully lower by end-2027 as tariff, energy shock and AI price pressures fade.
Goldman's eventual terminal rate forecast is unchanged at 3.25-3.50%. The hotter inflation path only delays the timing of cuts by one quarter.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Third consecutive upside surprise. The strength was broad-based and went beyond oil pass-through, which supports further Fed tightening.
Goldman's estimate implied by the CPI report. It points to firm inflation on the Fed's preferred gauge.
Goldman's forecast after a third 25bp hike. It is higher than its prior peak.
Unchanged by Goldman. Cuts are delayed by one quarter rather than reduced in size.
macro_indicators.period: after the cutting cycle (cuts through September 2028)

macro_indicators.reading: 25bp (Waller baseline); 50bp to be considered if core CPI was about 0.3% or higher
macro_indicators.interpretation: Waller's stated baseline and conditional alternative. Goldman thinks most voters will be reluctant to hike 50bp.

risk_factors: Inflation could stay firm into January ('January effect'), which would make a third hike the path of least resistance even if the energy shock has ended.
Broad-based core inflation strength beyond oil pass-through could push the Fed toward a 50bp December hike, as Waller suggested.
Goldman's forecast may be wrong if inflation stays firm after the energy pass-through fades, since tariff and AI-related price pressures may not diminish as expected.
geopolitical: Oil prices have fallen substantially since the elections, which Goldman says means most of the energy shock pass-through to consumer prices is behind us.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman sees the energy pass-through as largely behind us, with oil futures sharply lower since the elections and inflation meaningfully lower by end-2027. Cuts begin in December 2027 and the terminal rate stays at 3.25-3.50%.
tension_points.bear_case: Core CPI has surprised to the upside three months in a row on broad categories, going beyond oil. Waller floated a 50bp December hike. Firmer January inflation could make a third hike the path of least resistance.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Firmer January inflation data would make the third hike the path of least resistance even if the energy shock appears over.
